post_text: IS WALSALL COUNCIL ENFORCING ITS OWN POLICY ON SHOP DISPLAYS? ..IF NOT, WHY NOT? IF IT'S NOW DEEMED INAPPROPRIATE, THEN CHANGE IT! I have checked back through the records and it seems that the Council adopted a policy in 2009 "Criteria for shop displays and advertisements on the highway" (key extracts below). This policy was passed by the Licensing Committee on 9/10/2009 and agreed by full Council on 9/11/2009. (on public record if anyone wishes to check) Unless this policy has been superseded by a subsequent new/change of policy, then this policy should still prevail...... so my point is: If this policy is still in place, either enforce it or change/scrap the policy completely. *In law a highway is any way over which the public has a right to pass and repass, as of right, without hindrance EXTRACTS FROM COUNCIL POLICY “CRITERIA FOR SHOP DISPLAYS AND ADVERTISEMENTS ON THE HIGHWAY”, PASSED BY WALSALL COUNCIL LICENSING COMMITTEE ON 9/10/2009 AND AGREED BY FULL COUNCIL ON 9/11 2009. • All displays must be stable safe and not present any danger to the public and must not extend further than 0.5 metres from the shop frontage (unless the Highway Authority grants an exception) and must not be more than 1 metre high. Additionally, in all cases, at least 1.8 metres of clear pedestrian passageway is to be maintained. • Any trade display must consist of goods and materials which are not liable to be moved by external forces, such as the effects of the wind or from being lightly knocked. • Trade displays must not be erected before 7.00am and must be removed by 8.00pm. (unless there are traffic regulation orders in place which specify alternative times). • In all cases, displays are the sole responsibility of the individual business and the Council insists that third party public liability insurance be taken out to a minimum indemnity of £5,000,000. • In no cases must displays lead to excavations or damage of any kind to be made to the highway. • In no circumstances should any trade display interfere with required vision lines for traffic and / or pedestrians. • Goods on the highway are for display purposes only and items must not be sold from the highway. -------------------------------------------------------------------------- It is accepted that there are differences of opinion on this subject and this is to be respected.... that's a healthy part of a democratic process that should be welcomed by all. There is nothing unreasonable about asking our Council to clarify it's own policy, surely? Pete Smith. former Councillor, Blakenall ward.
post_summary: The discussion centres on a former councillor's demand for the enforcement or revision of Walsall Council’s 2009 shop display policy, contrasted with public criticism regarding the relevance of such regulations amidst broader economic and safety concerns.
